I am a 36-year-old farmer with no schooling. My family has 8 mu of land in Quzhou County, Hebei, and I have farmed this land since I was a teenager. Around here, every household grows winter wheat followed by summer maize — that is the only system that makes sense for our land, water, and climate on the North China Plain. I thought about cotton, but it needs sixteen or more pesticide sprays and too much hand labor, and with my family size I cannot manage it. Wheat and maize are reliable: the seed shops, fertilizer dealers, and grain buyers all come to our village.

This autumn, after National Day, I will plant improved wheat seeds on all 8 mu. Before sowing I will rotary till the soil to prepare a good seedbed. I will apply urea and compound fertilizer, about 6 kg of nitrogen per mu. I do not buy separate phosphate or potash — the compound fertilizer has a little, and our soil has always produced fine wheat without it. I will irrigate four times: once before winter, then at green-up, at jointing, and during grain filling. I will spray pesticides five times to control weeds, insects, and the diseases that always come when the weather turns humid.

In early June, right after the wheat harvest, I will immediately plant hybrid maize — I will buy Denghai or Nongda hybrids from the shop in town because they yield much better than ordinary seed. I will plant directly into the wheat stubble without tilling; this saves diesel and time, and everybody in the village does it now. I will not add extra nitrogen to the maize because the wheat fertilizer residue is still in the soil, and I will put down a little compound at planting. I will irrigate twice and spray pesticides about four times. That is my plan — simple, proven, and what I know works.
